zh: 一个角色的有效权限，等于它的直属权限并上所有父角色（被它继承的角色）的有效权限；父角色的有效权限又已经包含了更上层祖先的权限。授权图无环，所以只要保证“处理一个角色时它的所有父角色都已算完”，就能一层层推出来。重复授权边只是重复做一次并集，不影响结果。
先把所有出现过的权限串排序去重并编号，编号顺序就是要求的输出顺序，这样每个角色的集合可以用一个 P 位的位集表示，去重也是天然的。然后用 Kahn 算法按拓扑序处理：角色 u 入度变为 0 时，它的位集已是最终答案，再把它按位或到每个子角色上。每次合并只需 P/64 次字运算。
读入 n、m、各角色的直属权限和 m 条边 u→v（v 继承 u）。排序去重得到权限表，给每个角色建位集并置上直属权限对应的位；建邻接表和入度，入度为 0 的角色入队。依次出队 u，对每条边 u→v 做 bits[v] |= bits[u]，v 的入度减一、减到 0 就入队。最后对每个角色输出位集中 1 的个数，再按编号从小到大输出对应的权限串。输出可能达数千万字节，要用缓冲写出。
en: A role's effective permissions are its direct permissions united with the effective permissions of all its parent roles (the roles it inherits from), and a parent's effective permissions already include those of the ancestors above it. The grant graph is acyclic, so as long as every parent of a role has been finished before the role itself is processed, the sets can be derived level by level. Duplicate grants just repeat a union, which does not change the result.

First sort and deduplicate all permission strings that appear and number them; the numbering order is exactly the required output order, so each role's set can be a P-bit bitset, and deduplication comes for free. Then process the roles in topological order with Kahn's algorithm: when role u reaches in-degree 0, its bitset is already final, and it is ORed into each of its children. Each merge costs only P/64 word operations.

Read n, m, each role's direct permissions and the m edges u→v (v inherits u). Sort and deduplicate to get the permission table, build a bitset per role with the bits of its direct permissions set, and build the adjacency lists and in-degrees, enqueueing every role with in-degree 0. Pop roles u in turn; for each edge u→v do bits[v] |= bits[u], decrement v's in-degree, and enqueue v when it reaches 0. Finally, for each role print the number of set bits, then the matching permission strings in increasing index order. The output can be tens of millions of bytes, so write it through a buffer.

explanationEn:
## Problem

The effective permissions of each role = its own direct permissions ∪ the direct permissions of all its ancestor roles. A grant edge u→v means v inherits u; the graph is guaranteed to be acyclic, so the "ancestors" are determined by reachability along reversed edges. For each role, output its deduplicated permissions in lexicographic (ASCII) order.

## Approach: topological order + bitset merging

Sort and deduplicate all permission strings that appear, numbering them 0..P−1; the numbering order is exactly lexicographic order. Each role keeps a P-bit bitset of the permissions known so far, initialized to its direct permissions.

Process the roles in topological order with Kahn's algorithm: when a role u with in-degree 0 is taken out, all its parent roles have already been processed, so u's bitset is already the final answer; for each outgoing edge u→v, OR u's bitset into v and decrement v's in-degree.

When printing, enumerate the bits from low to high; the numbering order is lexicographic order, and duplicates are removed naturally.

## Correctness

By induction on the topological order: when u is dequeued, every w with an edge w→u has already been dequeued and merged its final set into u, so u's set equals its direct permissions ∪ the effective permissions of each parent role, and a parent's effective permissions in turn contain all of its own ancestors, so this is exactly the union over all of u's ancestors. Duplicate grant edges only repeat an idempotent union and do not affect the result.

## Complexity

Sorting the permission strings takes O(S log S), where S is the total number of direct permissions; each edge performs one bitset merge in O(P/64), for O(m·P/64) in total; output is proportional to the size of the answer. Merging hash sets element by element would reach O(m·P) insertions when there are many edges and many permissions, which is clearly slower.

## Independent verification

The oracle runs a BFS along reversed edges from each role to find all of its ancestors, then takes the union directly and sorts it, without using a topological order; large data are additionally computed with Python big-integer bitsets via memoized DFS over parent roles. All 25 labeled DAGs on 3 roles, combined with the four direct-permission choices {∅,A,a,Aa} for each role, are enumerated exhaustively, and the reference program is actually run on each one. The wrong programs (looking only at direct parents, merging edges in input order, reversing the direction of inheritance, and sorting case-insensitively) all exit normally and are judged wrong on the official data.
